intro: Here in Amasya province, along the Yeşilırmak, stand the Amasya Riverside Houses, from the 18th–19th century. A row of bow-fronted Ottoman houses lines the river, the rock tombs of the Pontic kings are cut into the cliff behind them, and the citadel hangs above.
history: The mansions lining the Yeşilırmak were built in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries, after the years when this city trained Ottoman princes. Look at their bays, overhanging the water. Behind the houses rise the rock-cut tombs of the Pontic kings, and above them, the citadel.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the riverside mansions and the Rock tombs of the Pontic kings. Look up to the Amasya citadel, step into the Hazeranlar Mansion, and find the Ferhat water channel.
facts: Did you know? The geographer Strabo was born here in 64 BC, and in the passage he gave to his native city he described both banks of the river. And the rock face behind the houses carries the monumental tombs of the Pontic kings: two thousand years separate the mansions from the graves.
outro: This brings our tour of Amasya Riverside Houses to an end. Before you go, a small request: please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. The river has watched these houses and tombs for centuries; let them wait for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
